# n8 - The CLI actually reaches the loop

n7's dogfood ran the three public verbs against an authored three-node scratch intent and found
that two of them never reach their own code. `runner step`, the verb the whole intent exists to
deliver, raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'opt_all' for module Runner` at
`scripts/runner:240` on every single invocation, before a sweep, an absorb or a dispatch ever
runs. `runner sweep` loads `RunnerSweep` and then falls through `dispatch_lazy`'s `case` to the
"no dispatcher is wired up yet" arm, because no `when "sweep"` was ever written.

Both slipped through five green node gates for the same reason: every runner test drives the
module API (`RunnerDispatch.dispatch`, `RunnerSweep.run`) and none drives `scripts/runner` itself
past argument parsing. The suite proved the engine and never turned the key.

So n8 is small in code and specific in tests. Define `opt_all`, the repeated-flag reader
`run_step` already assumes; add the missing `when "sweep"` arm; and pin the gap itself with a test
that walks `Runner::VERBS` and asserts that no declared verb reaches the fall-through arm, so the
next verb added without a dispatcher fails in CI rather than in someone's dogfood.

## n8 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.1 | Define `Runner.opt_all(args, name)`, returning every value given for a repeated flag | `run_step` calls it on line 240 and `runner step` dies with `NoMethodError` before any loop work runs, which is exactly what shipped | `runner_step_cli_test#test_step_runs_end_to_end_on_a_scratch_intent` |
| 8.2 | Return every occurrence, in order, not just the first or the last | Two `--return` pairs in one step silently absorb one node and drop the other, and the dropped node keeps its lease until it expires | `runner_step_cli_test#test_opt_all_returns_every_occurrence_in_order` |
| 8.3 | Return an empty array when the flag is absent | `each_with_object` is called on nil and a plain `runner step` with no returns raises instead of dispatching the first ready node | `runner_step_cli_test#test_opt_all_returns_empty_array_when_flag_absent` |
| 8.4 | Wire `when "sweep"` into `dispatch_lazy` | `runner sweep` prints "sweep's module loaded but no dispatcher is wired up yet" and exits 3, so the crash-recovery verb is unreachable from the CLI, which is exactly what shipped | `runner_cli_test#test_sweep_verb_reaches_runner_sweep` |
| 8.5 | Assert every verb in `Runner::VERBS` reaches a real dispatcher, not the fall-through arm | The next verb added to `VERBS` without a `when` arm ships unreachable the same way `sweep` did, and no test notices | `runner_cli_test#test_every_declared_verb_reaches_a_dispatcher` |
| 8.6 | Drive `scripts/runner step` end to end as a subprocess against a real armed scratch intent | Every runner test drives the module API and none turns the CLI key, which is how a `NoMethodError` on the intent's primary verb passed five green gates | `runner_step_cli_test#test_step_runs_end_to_end_on_a_scratch_intent` |
| 8.7 | Print the dispatch plan and exit 0 when a ready node exists | `step` reaches its own code and then produces nothing the session can spawn from, so the loop still does not run | `runner_step_cli_test#test_step_prints_a_dispatch_plan_for_a_ready_node` |
| 8.8 | Refuse a malformed `--return` pair with a message and a non-zero exit, never a raise | A typo in a return pair crashes the runner mid-step, after `running` lines are already written and before any of them is absorbed | `runner_step_cli_test#test_step_refuses_a_malformed_return_pair` |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code.
2. Define `opt_all` beside `opt`; add the `sweep` arm to `dispatch_lazy`.
3. Green, then the whole suite at its baseline.
